A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAD work, and their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison. V1's supplementary pages were inspected. V2 ends after its references; relocated supplementary content can be distinguished from material absent from the supplied PDF.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original Memory Maze and Minecraft experiments, computational measurements, and action-conditioning and memory-noise ablations.

after.justification: Sections 5–6 retain original experiments and add baseline comparisons, VBench evaluations and a partial-overlap ablation.

M1.justification: RAD retains its spatial/temporal attention, recurrent memory alternatives, overlapping frame-wise inference, clean-memory updates and hidden-state prefetching. The new Algorithms 1–2 document existing procedures. The stride-10 experiment tests a configuration rather than replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Memory Maze navigation and Minecraft action-conditioned video generation, with the same described evaluation scenarios. VBench metrics are applied to these retained datasets; they do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Tables 2–3 add Teacher Forcing and VRAG to both benchmark comparisons, substantially broadening the external comparator set beyond Diffusion Forcing. The existing recurrent variants remain. Identifying TTT-c as an implementation of LaCT does not introduce another evaluated method.

E3.justification: V2 adds five VBench evaluation dimensions covering background consistency, temporal flickering, motion smoothness, aesthetic quality and imaging quality. Section 6.2 also introduces a controlled stride-10 experiment with a 20-frame window during training and inference. Existing dataset splits and stated training budgets remain unchanged; the explicit Maze training-from-scratch statement is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: V2 adds the partial-overlap ablation and a component-level FLOPs analysis, but removes v1's action-conditioning ablation, PSNR-versus-frame curve and clean/noisy-memory training-loss plot. The memory-noise endpoint comparison remains. These changes substantially revise the supporting analyses and evidence for individual design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The added result tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds TF/VRAG results, VBench scores, stride-10 results and numerical FLOPs estimates, while removing action-ablation and curve results. Maze LSTM-f changes from PSNR 15.30 and LPIPS 0.50 in v1 Table 1 to 15.50 and 0.45 in v2 Table 2, with SSIM unchanged at 0.41. V2 Table 7 still reports the old clean-memory values without explaining the difference; other retained main benchmark rows are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 Table 6 adds analytical FLOPs expressions for the two-stage pipeline and its components. The RNN equations and asymptotic complexity comparison from v1 Appendix A.2 and Table 6 are retained in v2 Section 3.1 and Table 1; their relocation is not new theory.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain recurrent global memory combined with local attention, strong performance from simple LSTM blocks, improved continuity through overlapping frame-wise generation, and efficient attention through hidden-state prefetching. Rewritten framing and additional evidence do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 Section 7 newly acknowledges computational overhead and finite hidden-state capacity as limitations for very long contexts. Section 5.1 shifts from emphasizing SSIM for memory and PSNR/LPIPS for frame quality to treating all three as memory/consistency measures on the tailored tasks. Interpretations of the new analyses are added, while the main local/global-memory explanation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds training/inference pseudocode, explicit Maze initialization information and a project-page link. However, it omits v1's hyperparameter table, detailed memory-batching and tensor-shape instructions, and VAE checkpoints and input/latent dimensions from Appendix A.1/A.3/A.4. This substantially changes reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to the underlying settings or actual code availability.

R1.justification: VBench is newly cited, and v2 explicitly positions TTT-c as an implementation of the already cited LaCT work. The broader related-work coverage and positioning against context, hidden-state and weight-memory approaches remain substantially the same.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and memory-related-work paragraph are rewritten, with local clarifications elsewhere. Mamba/TTT explanations move from the supplement into the preliminaries. Most methodological and experimental prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, redraws Figure 1, rearranges attention diagrams, and adds algorithm boxes, a prefetching diagram and new tables. Existing benchmark tables are regrouped and the complexity table moves into the main text. The Maze visualization, action-ablation table, PSNR curve and training-loss plot disappear; several captions expand.

improvement.justification: V2 improves comparison breadth through TF/VRAG and VBench, adds a useful overlap ablation, clarifies procedures and states concrete limitations. These gains coexist with substantial loss of reproducibility details and action-conditioning evidence. The unexplained discrepancy between Maze LSTM-f results in Tables 2/8 and the clean-memory results in Table 7 also weakens internal consistency. The supplied PDFs therefore show material benefits and harms without a reliably clear net quality improvement.
